newsitem.title: USA: US OCC issues rule on bank securities investments.
newsitem.headline: US OCC issues rule on bank securities investments.

text.p: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said Monday it approved a rule that will expand the amount a bank can invest in certain types of mortgage and asset-backed securities.
The rule implements provisions of the Riegle Community Development and Regulatory Improvement Act of 1994 and creates two new regulatory designations of securities, Type IV and V.

In the Type IV category, the rule allows banks to invest without limit in residential and commercial mortgage-related securities if they are rated investment grade by a nationally recognized rating organization.
Banks also would have no limit for investing in securities related to small businesses if they are rated in the top two rating categories, the bank regulator said.

If the small business securities are rated in the third or fourth-highest rating category, a bank's investment in securities of any one issuer would be limited to 25 percent of capital and surplus, the OCC said.

Type V securities encompass asset-backed securities formed from an underlying pool of loans, such as automobile or credit card loans. The new rule sets a limit on bank investments in those securities at 25 percent of capital.
Prior to the final rule, which affects national banks and goes into effect Dec. 31, bank investments in Type IV and V securities was limited to 10 percent of capital, an OCC spokesman said.
